sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P., Thru. Its Prin. Secy., Home Deptt., Lko. And Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Ram Pheran Dwivedi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Karunesh Singh Pawar,J.
1.Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State and perused the record.
None appears for the complainant in spite of service of notice.
2. It is alleged in the first information report that the minor daughter of the informant has been enticed away by the applicant on 21.5.2023 at about 6.00a.m..
3.Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated.
The prosecutrix is major.
In the ossification test, she has been found to be 17 years of age.

1 I take judicial notice of the fact that the margin of error in age ascertained by radiological examination is two years on either side as held by Supreme Court in Jaya Mala versus Home Secretary, Government of Jammu & Kashmir and others (1982)2 SCC 538.

entities.text: Jaya Mala versus Home Secretary, Government of Jammu & Kashmir and others (1982)2 SCC 538
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant being the accused is entitled for giving the benefit on higher side.
The victim in her statement under section 161 CrPC has not supported the prosecution version.
She on her own accord went away with the applicant.
There is no physical injury found in the medical nor there is any corroborative evidence found in the medical examination of the victim.
The applicant has no previous criminal history.
The applicant is in jail since 11.8.2023.
It is further submitted that there is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away after being released on bail or tampering with the witnesses.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
4.Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the aforesaid facts as argued by the learned counsel for the applicant.

5.Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, statement of the victim recorded under sections 161 and 164 CrPC, the applicant has no criminal history, arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, the applicant is in jail since 11.8.2023, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am prima facie satisfied that it is a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail and accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
6.Let the applicant Sheru alias Noor Babu involved in Case Crime No.0156/2023 under section 363 I.P.C., after investigation increases the offence under sections 363, 376(3) I.P.C. and 3/4 POCSO Act, P.S. Dargah Sharif, district Bahraich, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.

(iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

sentences.text: (v) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(vi) In case the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
7. Observation(s) made herein above shall not be considered as an expression of opinion on merit of the case.
